name: Google Fonts weighted tags (google/fonts tags/all/families.csv and quant.csv; the same tags through the Developer API, capability=FAMILY_TAGS)
what_it_is: Plain CSVs in github.com/google/fonts/tags/all, one row per `family, axis-position, tag path, score`. families.csv (34,163 rows; its README calls it 'human assessed') holds 0-100 scores for 74 tag paths in 11 groups: Expressive 20 (Active, Loud, Calm, Futuristic, Vintage, Rugged...), Theme 15 (Techno, Pixel, Stencil, Brush, Wacky...), Sans 7, Serif 7, Slab 3, Script 4, Seasonal 8, Quality 4 (Drawing, Spacing, Concept, Wordspace), Purpose 2, Special use 3, Monospace 1. 22,533 rows are family-level (1,939 families); 11,630 rows are per variable-axis position (e.g. wght@700). quant.csv (19,236 rows, 'machine assessed') gives measured stroke_width_min/max per weight position and opsz_min/max for 1,977 families (range 0-1000 per tags_metadata.csv). skip.csv flags 121 families whose stroke width is not computed. tags_metadata.csv lists the tag paths (all 0-100, quant 0-1000); tags_ui_details.textproto defines Google's own filter groups (Feeling 19, Appearance 18, Serif 9, Sans 8, Calligraphy 5, Technology 2, Seasonal 2) and contains no score thresholds. Zero scores are left out of the CSV (tag-tool issue google/fonts#8506: Space/Backspace 'marks a family as zero-valued (excluded from CSV output)'), so a missing row means 'zero or not yet assessed' [uncertain: which of the two, per tag].
provider_and_url: Google Fonts team. Tags are edited through a 'tag tool' (issues #8506, #9210, #8514); recent commits are tag-by-tag passes ('Update families.csv Tag Playful'). Files: https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/tags ; raw: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/tags/all/families.csv ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/tags/all/quant.csv . Developer API: https://developers.google.com/fonts/docs/developer_api (needs an API key; with capability=FAMILY_TAGS each family gets tags:[{name, weight}] for the whole design space). I could not call the API (no key), so whether it returns exactly the family-level CSV rows is unverified.
catalog_coverage: Measured by me: SCRATCH/families.csv joined by exact family name to the app's merged catalog, which I rebuilt from server/.cache/remote-v7.json plus server/data/*.json with the same priority/dedupe rule (reproduces 2,099 rows and the 1,760/64/63/26/23/163 split exactly). Google source: 1,613 of 1,760 rows (91.6%) have family-level tags. The 147 without are 116 rows that are not Google families at all (Fontsource type 'other': Fusion Pixel 24, Fusion Kai 3, DSEG 11, DejaVu, Adwaita, Commit Mono, Comic Mono...) plus 31 real Google families, of which roughly 15-19 are renames where the catalog still carries Fontsource's old name next to the new one (Fredoka One / Fredoka, Source Sans Pro / Source Sans 3, Big Shoulders Display / Big Shoulders, Merienda One / Merienda, BBH Sans Bartle / BBH Bartle...). Of true Google families: 1,613 of 1,644 (98.1%). Fontshare 0 of 64, Velvetyne 0 of 63, Collletttivo 0 of 26, Tunera 0 of 23, Use & Modify 0 of 163 (a Google family that Fontshare or Use & Modify also carry shows up as a Google row). Rows carrying Google tags overall: 1,613 of 2,099 (76.8%). The claim '1,936 of 1,980 Fontsource Google families': I count 1,941 of 1,980 Fontsource type-'google' families by exact name (98.0%); the CSV has 1,941 distinct family names. quant.csv matches 1,629 of the 1,760 Google rows. Rows whose prompt tags survive the app's own filter: 1,598 (15 tagged families have nothing at 40 or above).
granularity: Per family (22,533 rows), plus per variable-axis position for 388 of the 1,613 matched catalog families (11,630 rows, mostly wght@100..900, some wdth/opsz). Of 3,385 tag series that have two or more positions, 398 (12%) move by 30 points or more across positions (for example a mood stronger at wght 900), so a few families have weight-dependent mood. Nothing per italic style.
signal_type: Semantic mood (Expressive), visual theme or genre (Theme and the Sans/Serif/Slab/Script subclasses) and, in quant.csv, measured geometry (stroke width). All on one 0-100 scale, except quant.
mood_dimensions_covered: All counts are catalog Google families (1,613) with the tag at 40 or above, measured by me from families.csv. MOTION/ACTIVE (weak): Active 110 (6.8%; 71 at 60+), Excited 180. The Active tag mostly means lively pen writing, not speed: 60 of the 110 are Fontsource 'handwriting', 74 carry a Script tag at 40+. Top Active: Faster One 94, Aguafina Script 93, Story Script 91, Vujahday Script 90, Arizonia 90, Kaushan Script 89. Only about 15 are speed-like (Faster One 94, Kablammo 84, Train One 73, Contrail One 72, Racing Sans One 71, Climate Crisis 71, Fugaz One 60). Techno-looking faces mostly have no Active row: Exo 2 (none; only Vintage 10), Saira (no Expressive row), Teko (Vintage 25, Loud 4), Saira Extra Condensed (Active 10), Bebas Neue (Active none). Tiny oracle I built from description evidence (17 fonts whose designer text says speed, fast curves, momentum, action or sport): Active at 40+ finds 8 of 17, Active or Excited 9, Active, Excited, Futuristic or Techno 12. Rows with no Active or Excited row at all: RocknRoll One, Rowdies, Playball. The oracle comes from the descriptions, so it is small and slightly circular. LOUD (strong): 154 (113 are display); tracks measured stroke weight (r=0.83 with quant stroke width at wght 400, n=1,394). FUTURISTIC/TECHNO (good): Futuristic 97, Techno 80; 12 of the 15 families whose designer text says futuristic, sci-fi or spaceship have Futuristic or Techno at 40+ (misses Exo, Exo 2, Azeret Mono). CALM 255, PLAYFUL 256, HAPPY 150, CUTE 120, CHILDLIKE 77, BUSINESS 307, COMPETENT 188 and SINCERE 392 (these two are not in Google's own filter UI), SOPHISTICATED 61, FANCY 76, ARTISTIC 189, INNOVATIVE 78, STIFF 145, AWKWARD 402; VINTAGE (815) and RUGGED (723) are so broad (50% and 45% of families) that at 40 they hardly discriminate. ELEGANT: Sophisticated + Fancy + Script/Formal + Serif/Didone. HANDMADE: Script/Handwritten and Informal, Theme/Brush 57. Theme: Pixel 43, Stencil 13, Inline 12, Art Deco 10, Wacky 68, Blobby 17. NOT COVERED: speed or racing as such, sporty, angular, organic, minimal, 'bold' (only via the measured stroke width).
query_style_specificity: Better for tight requests that match one of the 35 mood and theme tags (techno, pixel, stencil, brush, calm, playful, loud) than for loose or compound ones. 'Fast movement or action' maps to four or five weak candidates (Active, Excited, Futuristic, Techno, Loud) and the model has to pick among them; in my 17-font oracle those cover 12 at best. 'Friendly' and 'professional' map to many broad tags (Happy, Cute, Business, Competent) and work reasonably because those tags are populated.
quality_evidence: I did NOT run a live LLM A/B test (it would spend subscription quota); everything below is measured offline by me. (1) quant.csv stroke width at wght 400 correlates r=0.83 with the Loud score over 1,394 catalog families (min stroke over weights 0.80, max 0.47), so the human mood tag and the machine measurement agree. (2) Legacy slant (mean of upright styles, site metadata) correlates r=0.51 with Active (Pearson; Spearman 0.42; n=712), still r=0.53 outside handwriting (n=590); legacy thickness (mean over styles) r=0.73 with Loud (n=714; the outline claimed 0.77). Futuristic and Techno correlate at most 0.10 with width, slant, thickness or stroke: the tags carry information shape measurements cannot recover. (3) Agreement with designer text: 12 of 15 'futuristic/sci-fi' descriptions get Futuristic or Techno at 40+; names containing Stencil: 3 of 8 get Theme/Stencil at 40+ (misses Big Shoulders Stencil x3, Saira Stencil x2, which are unrated or renamed); names containing Pixel or Bitcount: 16 of 16 Google families get Theme/Pixel at 40+ (the 24 Fusion Pixel rows are not Google families and have no tags). (4) Google uses the same tags in its own Feeling and Appearance filters (tags_ui_details.textproto). (5) Contradictions are rare: Calm with Loud, Excited or Active at 60+: 0 families each. Counter-evidence: Active is script-heavy, so Active at 40+ finds only about half of my motion oracle. No published retrieval evaluation of this CSV found; the related datasets (MyFonts, O'Donovan) belong to other items.
known_noise: Seasonal tags are the worst: 170 of 1,613 families (10.5%) have some Seasonal tag at 80+, Hanukkah at 80+ on 17 families (Kaushan Script 92, Bungee 94, Varela Round, Great Vibes), Valentine's, Holi, Diwali similar. The app already drops Seasonal, so this noise never reaches the prompt. Quality tags are not discriminating (every family has all four; medians Concept 70, Drawing 68, Spacing 70, Wordspace 90) and the app drops them too. Absence is ambiguous: Exo 2, Saira and Teko have no Active (nor Futuristic or Techno) row although Exo's own designer text says 'technological/futuristic' and Michroma has Active 10 next to Futuristic 94; since zeros are omitted and tags are still being added tag by tag (100 commits on families.csv from 2026-03-05 to 2026-09-23), some gaps are probably 'not assessed' [uncertain]. Mild contradictions: Happy with Awkward both at 60+ on 35 families, Futuristic with Vintage on 17. Vintage and Rugged at 40+ cover about half of all families. 18 rows carry non-integer scores (10.5, 92.6), which a strict integer parse rejects (I hit this myself; the app's Number() is fine). About 15-19 catalog rows use a retired Fontsource name and get no tags (and the new name also sits in the catalog, so Haiku can see a duplicate).
name_and_memory_bias: Tags remove some name dependence but not all. Racing Sans One scores Active 71 and Loud 62, yet its designer text is a history of 1800s high-contrast sans; only the tag and the name say 'racing'. Orbitron/Audiowide/Iceland score Techno 100, Futuristic 88-92, which is also what the model already remembers from fonts.google.com, where these tags are displayed. So popular, well-known techno faces would be found with or without the tags; the tags help most for lesser-known families. The 'very common' demotion in vibe.ts is a separate guard against popularity.
untagged_rows: Not pushed down by code (catalog order is source band, then 'very common' last, then popularity rank), but a model that matches tag words has nothing to match: 410 of 1,760 Google-source rows (23%) show no mood or theme tag in the prompt, 137 rows have no tag at all, and 345 of 2,099 rows (16%) have one tag or none. Correction to the brief: of those 345, 336 are Google-source rows (97 are non-Google Fontsource families; the rest are Google families the CSV lacks, renamed, or tags under 40) and 9 are Use & Modify. Velvetyne (median 7 tags), Collletttivo (8) and Tunera (7) all have at least 3 tags, and Fontshare has a median of 4, but in their own vocabularies (brutalist, wonky, pixel, Posters, Magazines), so Google's mood words never match them. The ~340 thin rows are mostly NOT indie or Fontshare.
text_interference_risk: Not applicable: tags and numbers, nothing is rendered.
integration_path: ALREADY IN THE APP: server/catalog.ts parseGoogleTags (around line 385) reads family-level rows only, keeps score >= 40, drops Quality, Seasonal and Purpose groups, keeps the top 6 by score, labels subclasses as 'Geometric sans' / 'Formal script', discards the scores, and adds 'Slab' from the site metadata stroke field. The result sits in tags[] and is printed by compactCatalog in server/vibe.ts as `Family | category | sources | Active, Artistic, Happy`. NOT USED: the scores, tags under 40 or beyond six, the axis-position rows, quant.csv, skip.csv, Purpose (Easy Reading, Learn To Write), Special use (Barcode, Redaction, Symbols, worth using to EXCLUDE rows), aliases for renamed families. PATH 1 (cheap, extra catalog field): keep scores and print `Active 89, Artistic 97` (same row order, fully deterministic, so the cached prompt stays cacheable). Add an alias map for renamed families (slug-prefix match plus a short hand list) and join to the 1,613 matched rows. PATH 2 (precomputed data file plus a scoring step before the LLM): write server/data/google-tags.json = {"Faster One": {"Active":94,"Excited":30,"Loud":34,"Rugged":..}, ...} (about 1,613 families x ~7 tags, roughly 250 KB), and a second tiny file with quant stroke width at wght 400. A first Haiku call turns the request into weights over Google's 35 mood/theme terms, e.g. {"Active":1,"Excited":0.6,"Futuristic":0.4,"Techno":0.3}; plain code ranks every row with score = sum(weight * s/100), unrated = 0, keeps the top ~80 plus every indie row (which has no Google tags), and the main call sees only the shortlist. PATH 3 (re-rank after the LLM): keep today's call, then boost picks whose Google scores match the mapped weights. For the indie rows a vocabulary bridge is needed (foundry word -> Google tag) or measured traits; that is the indie-gap item.
tokens_per_row: Measured by me: today's catalog text is 163,390 characters for 2,099 rows (77 per row), about 41k tokens at 4 characters per token. Adding `:score` to each retained tag costs about 19,000 characters, roughly 6-9k tokens in total (about 3-4 tokens per tagged row, +15%). It stays cacheable because it is static between searches. Path 2 removes most of the catalog from the main prompt (a shortlist of ~80 rows is about 2-3k tokens).
vocabulary_alignment: It IS the shared vocabulary: 20 Expressive + 15 Theme terms plus classification tags. Google's own UI exposes 18 of the 20 Expressive tags (not Competent or Sincere). The indie sources use their own ~50 keywords (brutalist, wonky, inktraps...), Fontshare uses use-case tags (Posters, Magazines, Branding) and the app's rows from Collletttivo are tagged by hand by the app author, so nothing outside Google maps onto it yet.
explainability: Yes: a result can say 'Futuristic 92, Techno 100 (Google Fonts tag)', a number a person can check on fonts.google.com. quant stroke width adds a measured value.
determinism: The data and a code-side score are deterministic. Today's final choice stays non-deterministic because Haiku picks from the catalog; with Path 2 the shortlist is deterministic for a given weight vector.
build_effort: Path 1: about half a day, mostly in server/catalog.ts (keep scores, alias map) and server/vibe.ts (print them), plus a unit test that a renamed family picks up its tags and a regression check on the cached remote-v*.json bump (RULES_VERSION). Path 2: 2-3 days (weights prompt, scorer, shortlist merge with indie rows, evaluation grid). An agent can do both without new dependencies; the data is already fetched by the catalog build.
per_search_cost_and_latency: Path 1: no extra call; +6-9k input tokens on a ~41k-token cached system prompt (cache reads are 0.1x the input price on the API; on the subscription it is quota, not dollars). Path 2: one extra short Haiku call (about 1-2 s, a few hundred tokens) plus <10 ms of code scoring over 2,099 rows, and a main prompt of a few thousand tokens instead of ~41k, which should make the main call faster (the code comment in vibe.ts measured ~7 s for a follow-up with thinking off) [uncertain: not measured by me].
one_off_cost: Nothing beyond downloading the CSVs (families.csv 1.36 MB, quant.csv 0.96 MB; both already in the scratch folder). The app fetches families.csv on each catalog build already.
human_effort: About 1 hour first time: check the alias map (~20 names) and the request-to-tag vocabulary (35 terms). Close to zero as the catalog grows, apart from new renames.
asset_access: Public and key-free: raw.githubusercontent.com serves both CSVs (the app already requests families.csv in server/catalog.ts, one request per catalog rebuild). The Developer API needs an API key, adds nothing the CSV lacks that I could verify, and is not needed.
licence_and_provenance: Unclear for the tag data [uncertain]. The google/fonts repo has no root LICENSE (GitHub API reports licence null; /LICENSE and /tags/LICENSE return 404); its README says 'the top-level directories indicate the license of all files found within them', and /tags has no licence file. The 'CC BY 4.0' in the brief traces to the Developer API docs page, which says the page content is CC BY 4.0 (and code samples Apache 2.0); that statement is about the documentation text and I found nothing extending it to the tag values. Practical read: Google publishes the files openly in a public repo and shows the tags on fonts.google.com; using them in a local personal app is low risk; republishing a derived tag table in the app's public static build would be safer with a credit line to Google Fonts. Font licences (OFL / Apache / Ubuntu UFL for Google families) matter only for derived images, which this item does not make.
etiquette: One static-file request per catalog rebuild from GitHub raw; no robots or bot protection concern; the API would need a key under Google's API terms. Velvetyne is not involved.
maintenance_and_freshness: Active and growing: 100 commits to families.csv between 2026-03-05 and 2026-09-23 (about 15 a month, newest 2026-09-23), quant.csv 13 commits since 2025-06-25 (newest 2026-09-21); PR #10841 (2026-09-04) completed Loud for wdth and wght variable fonts. The tag-tool issue states the aim to be 'library-complete' for some tags. Work to keep current: none for the pull (the app refetches); new Google families arrive untagged (31 true Google families in today's catalog have no rows), so alias and gap handling should run at every build. Because tagging is in progress, scores for a family may shift between pulls and the cached prompt changes when they do.
risks_and_limitations: (1) Active is not 'fast': it is dominated by script and handwriting, so a 'fast movement' search that trusts Active returns calligraphy; speed needs slant, width and the designer text as well. (2) Missing may mean zero or not yet assessed. (3) Only Google families are tagged; 23% of the catalog (all 275 indie rows, 64 Fontshare rows, 116 non-Google Fontsource rows) gets nothing from this item. (4) Adding scores makes a model lean harder on literal tag words, which the INSTRUCTIONS in vibe.ts explicitly warn against for indie rows. (5) Licence of the data is undocumented. (6) The CSV is a moving target; scores and coverage changed in the last six months. (7) Renamed families make duplicate rows in the catalog (Fredoka One and Fredoka). (8) My oracle and correlations are small and offline; there is no live A/B result.
evaluation_hook: Hold out one tag (say Active or Techno) for a random 20% of tagged families and recover it from the other tags plus measured stroke width; a rated grid of result sets for 20-30 mood and motion queries with and without scores; and my 17-font motion oracle as a smoke test (today: Active at 40+ finds 8 of 17).
recommendation_for_font_explorer: USE IT, mostly as it is, and extend it a little; do not expect it to solve 'fast movement'. It is already half in the app (6 tags per family, no scores) and covers 1,613 of the 1,644 true Google families, so the remaining gain is small and cheap: (a) keep the scores in the prompt, (b) map the ~15-19 renamed families so they stop showing as untagged, (c) use quant stroke width as a free 'heavy/light' number (r=0.83 with Loud). Relative to the other items: it is the best source for tech, pixel, stencil, brush, calm, playful and loud, and the weakest for motion; for motion the designer descriptions (82% of Google rows have one) and measured slant/width fill more of the gap, and for the 275 indie rows only measured traits, vision labels or tag transfer can help, since this item gives them nothing. It is also the shared vocabulary any transfer scheme (the indie-gap item) would predict into. SMALLEST FIRST STEP: in server/catalog.ts parseGoogleTags, return `Active 89`-style strings (keep the existing >= 40 and top-6 rules), add an alias map for the renamed families, bump the catalog rules version, and run the 20-30 query grid once with and without scores. About half a day.
